title: WEF SmartStart final public verification — depth 5
summary: The recursive path reaches its configured maximum depth with New York confirmed only at broad granularity, exact implementation details undisclosed, a curriculum grade-range conflict and several documented false-positive collisions.

data.question: What can be verified publicly about SmartStart's exact New York implementation at maximum recursion depth?
data.method: Bounded official-source, public professional-source, New York education, procurement, vendor and adjacent-industry search with negative-result logging.
data.framework: Implementation verification with false-positive control and source-conflict preservation.
data.scope: SmartStart USA New York school, funding, curriculum and vendor implementation.
findings: WEF confirms an August 2026 pilot in a partner U.S. high school and separately says the initiative is launching in New York, but does not name the school or resolve city versus state.
R4203 shows that funding mapping and portal development were active implementation tasks, not evidence of a completed award or selected vendor.
A public WEF contributor describes a 60-plus-organization collective and names contributors, but this does not identify the pilot school or each organization's formal role.
Carol O'Donnell says SSEC contributed to a grades 10-12 three-year framework, while Soulaima Gourani describes grades 11-12.
Micron's Central New York workforce and education investments are a strong adjacent manufacturing-education graph but remain unconnected to SmartStart on reviewed evidence.
NYSED Smart Start and NYC SmartStart Education are unrelated name collisions.
conclusions: The strongest defensible result is a bounded negative:exact public implementation details remain undisclosed as of the search date.
No reviewed evidence supports naming Micron, NYSED Smart Start grantees or SmartStart Education as SmartStart USA implementers.
The curriculum grade range is unresolved and should not be normalized to a single value.
The recursive path should stop at max depth and reopen only on new primary evidence.
recommendations: Watch for an official school, district, agreement, award, curriculum specification or portal privacy notice after the August 2026 launch.
Do not broaden into candidate identity research.
Retain New York and Central New York adjacency as leads, not conclusions.
counterarguments: The school may have been intentionally withheld before launch.
A private implementation agreement or unindexed board agenda may already exist.
Micron's regional education stack could overlap operationally without public attribution.
limitations: The pilot date was still in the future on the search date.
LinkedIn contributor claims are not equivalent to official programme specifications.

caveats: Negative search result is bounded by time and indexing coverage.

workflow.next_action: Stop at configured maximum depth; reopen only on new primary evidence.
